diagnosis.root_cause: CRM marks customer 19426 inactive, but the RADIUS record remains serviceable because no Framed-Pool restriction was applied; the subscriber is still assigned IP 10.5.50.188 and passing traffic.
evidence: The subscriber is marked active: 0 and deleted: 0 in CRM.
The subscriber is nevertheless online, authenticated, assigned 10.5.50.188, and generating traffic.
The RADIUS record exists and matches the subscriber line ID, so this is not a missing-entry or line-ID conflict.
RADIUS diagnostics explicitly report disabled_not_pooled: CRM suspension was not applied because Framed-Pool is null.
The assigned address is in 10.5.50.0/24, which identifies a suspended-but-still-served customer.
The optical link is healthy: RX is normal at approximately -22.4 dBm, TX is normal at approximately +2.3 dBm, distance is stable, and bias current is stable.
The ONU and all sampled peers on EPON0/4 are online, ruling out ONU, splitter, PON-port, OLT, and shared physical faults.
The OLT, router, VLAN, authentication exchange, and session rate are otherwise normal.

remediation.action: Apply the suspension in RADIUS by setting the appropriate non-service or suspended pool/restriction, terminate the active session, and verify that the customer can no longer obtain service. Reconcile the CRM and RADIUS provisioning workflow so inactive customers cannot retain a normal address-pool assignment.

ground_truth.root_cause: The customer is marked inactive in CRM but RADIUS never applied the suspension. Framed-Pool is unset and the assigned address is in pool_Users, so full service continues. This is one of the 218 such cases in the estate.
expected_reasoning: CRM marks the customer inactive, which should mean service is suspended
RADIUS has a radcheck row with no Framed-Pool set
A suspended customer should be assigned to pool_Disable_Users and hold an address in 10.200.200.0/24
The assigned address is 10.5.50.188, which is in pool_Users, the standard subscriber range
The IP range settles the question without relying on either system's status flag
Sessions are active with a 715 minute mean and traffic is normal across all seven days
The customer is therefore receiving full service despite being suspended in CRM
The optical layer is healthy and irrelevant to this fault
There is no service impact for the customer; the impact is commercial
distractors: Every technical signal is healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
No customer has complained and none will
service_impact is false even though a genuine fault exists
